columns.rationale: Two-letter IATA carrier code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 equal to the row_count of 16, making it a natural unique key (samples: 9E, AA, DL, UA, WN).
Full airline name with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 (samples: Delta Air Lines Inc., JetBlue Airways); renamed from the generic 'name' to carrier_name for clarity in downstream joins.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true in the profile; a capture-tool record identifier with no business meaning.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; a single extraction timestamp (min = max = 2026-09-02T23:26:17) carrying pipeline provenance only.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 1 with the only value '{}', an empty capture-tool metadata payload.

decisions.rationale: carrier has distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so one row per two-letter carrier code is the smallest defensible grain; carrier_name also shows 16 distinct values but the code is the conventional join key.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 16, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe strategy is applied.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true in the profile and carry only pipeline provenance (_airbyte_meta is uniformly '{}'), so they are dropped from silver.
The bronze column 'name' is too generic for a lookup table consumed via joins; renamed to carrier_name to be self-describing alongside the carrier code.

purpose: silver_nyc_airlines is a cleaned carrier lookup dimension mapping the two-letter IATA carrier code to the full airline name, sourced from bronze.nyc_airlines. It feeds joins from flight-level fact tables that carry only the carrier code.
usage: Join on carrier (the declared grain and primary key) to enrich flight records with carrier_name. All 16 rows are complete: both columns have null_rate 0.0, so no null filtering is needed. Treat the table as a slowly changing reference set refreshed on each pipeline run.
limitations: The table reflects a single extraction (all rows extracted at 2026-09-02T23:26:17) and covers only the 16 carriers present in the source; carriers absent from the source period will not resolve in joins. No historical name changes or carrier mergers are tracked, and Airbyte capture metadata was dropped, so bronze must be consulted for lineage at the row level.
